official.deadline_note: No deadline is published for this scholarship: it is invitation-only, with the Advice Center for Study Funding inviting students after the HSG Assessment Year. The 1 October (autumn semester) and 1 March (spring semester) deadlines printed on the same official page apply to the means-tested HSG Loan and Scholarship Fund and to tuition-fee remission applications, not to this excellence scholarship.
official.status_note: The official page states that currently the University of St.Gallen and the Monique Dornonville de la Cour - Stiftung award scholarships for excellence at the Bachelor level in cooperation with the Advice Center for Study Funding. There is no application window because candidates are identified and invited after the Assessment Year.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship amount corresponds to the current tuition fees at the Bachelor level for a total of 6 semesters. Per HSG's Costs of an HSG degree page, Bachelor tuition fees as of autumn semester 2026 are CHF 1,310.50 per semester for Swiss nationals and CHF 3,343.50 per semester for foreign nationals.

official.description: The University of St.Gallen awards Excellence Scholarships to students enrolled in a Bachelor's degree on the basis of merit, with the scholarship amount corresponding to the current Bachelor-level tuition fees for a total of six semesters. The scholarships are currently awarded by the University of St.Gallen together with the Monique Dornonville de la Cour - Stiftung in cooperation with the Advice Center for Study Funding. It is not open to self-application: the Advice Center for Study Funding identifies enrolled students with outstanding academic performance in the HSG Assessment Year and invites them to apply.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply for this scholarship: HSG's Advice Center for Study Funding screens Assessment Year results and invites outstanding students to apply, and an unsolicited application is not possible. If invited, the award covers the Bachelor tuition fee for the remaining six semesters at the rate current when it is granted - worth CHF 3,343.50 per semester for foreign nationals and CHF 1,310.50 for Swiss nationals as of autumn semester 2026 - but nothing else. Living costs of roughly CHF 25,000-30,000 per year remain your responsibility, so treat this as a tuition-fee waiver, not a full ride. The practical lever you control is your Assessment Year performance, plus keeping your contact details current at HSG so an invitation reaches you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled HSG Bachelor students with top Assessment Year grades, above all foreign nationals, since the award offsets the higher non-Swiss tuition rate and they still need separate living-cost funding.
application_readiness_checklist: Prioritise grades in the HSG Assessment Year: that performance is the screening basis for invitations
Keep your address and email current at HSG, because the invitation comes from the Advice Center for Study Funding, not through a public portal
Watch for the invitation after Assessment Year results and respond quickly, since the page publishes no fixed window
Plan living-cost funding separately (about CHF 2,175 per month / CHF 13,050 per semester), as the award covers tuition only

If you want a foundation scholarship you can apply for directly, check the Swiss Study Foundation and the German Academic Scholarship Foundation, which HSG recommends and which accept self-applications
common_rejection_risks: Never entering the pool because Assessment Year performance was not judged outstanding - selection happens by screening, not by open competition
Assuming the 1 October / 1 March deadlines apply here; they govern the means-tested HSG Loan and Scholarship Fund and fee-remission applications
Budgeting on the assumption the award covers living costs, leaving a gap of roughly CHF 25,000-30,000 per year
Losing the award mid-degree through weaker later performance, since further selection criteria may be applied depending on the funding source
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs of about CHF 2,175 per month (CHF 13,050 per semester, per HSG's own table), plus the non-refundable CHF 268 application and processing fee; HSG recommends budgeting CHF 25,000-30,000 per year in total.
document_audit: There is no document checklist to prepare, because the scholarship has no open application - the means-testing documents (tax documentation and similar) described on the same page apply to the HSG Loan and Scholarship Fund
Keep Assessment Year transcripts and grade records at hand in case the committee requests them after the invitation arrives
alerts: Invitation-only: an application without an invitation from the University of St.Gallen is not possible, so there is nothing to submit in advance
The value tracks the fee in force at award time, not a fixed sum: autumn semester 2026 rates are CHF 1,310.50 per semester (Swiss nationals) and CHF 3,343.50 per semester (foreign nationals)
Current funders are the University of St.Gallen and the Monique Dornonville de la Cour - Stiftung, so the applicable additional selection criteria can change with the funding source
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The Advice Center for Study Funding identifies invitees after the Assessment Year and invites them to apply; invited students submit their application to the university and the relevant committees make the final award decision.
